 Media ‘Star Wars’ animated alt-cast latest addition for Disney/ESPN at Super Bowl LXI
 By Austin Karp 10.19.2026 Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} "Star Wars Funday Football" will be the Super Bowl's first animated alt-cast. ESPN In a win for scruffy-looking nerf herders, Super Bowl LXI will be the first Big Game to feature a dedicated animated alt-cast, with ESPN, Lucasfilm and the NFL bringing audiences to the world of “Star Wars” on Feb. 14.
 A formal announcement came in the form of a video shown at halftime of the Commanders-49ers “Monday Night Football” game.
 Disney Channel and DisneyXD will be the linear channels involved for “Star Wars Funday Football,” while Disney+ will stream the alt-cast, which once again will tap into Sony’s Beyond Sports to create the data visualization technology.
 Beyond Sports is the company behind previous animated efforts for “MNF” set in the worlds of “ Toy Story ,” “ The Simpsons ” and “ Monsters, Inc. ” The Sony division has also worked with ESPN and Disney on an animated NBA “ Dunk the Halls ” telecast on Christmas Day, as well as NHL games within the worlds of “ Inside Out ” and “ Big City Greens .” Beyond Sports last year extended its deal with ESPN to do more animated alt-casts.
 Additional details are to be announced in the coming months, including which announcers will call the animated game and in what “Star Wars” environments the game will be played (a graphic promoting the game hints at the fictional desert planet of Tatooine). ESPN’s Drew Carter has called all three animated “MNF” games, and Dan Orlovsky was the analyst around “Monsters, Inc.” last year. One voice that “Star Wars” fans will recognize during the game is actor Anthony Daniels , who voices C-3PO.
 The 2025 effort was also the first time an NFL animated alt-cast had sold separate advertiser deals. While Disney Ad Sales has said the game is sold out , the company earlier this month also said it was creating a backup list of potential advertisers .
 This latest addition -- the last planned alt-cast for Super Bowl LXI -- gives ESPN and Disney its latest way to consume the game, including:
 ESPN : Main telecast
 ABC : Simulcast of main telecast
 ESPN2 : “ManningCast” alt-cast
 ESPNU : “Field Pass with The Pat McAfee Show” alt-cast
 NFL Network : “Playbook with Next Gen Stats” alt-cast
 Disney Channel / Disney XD : “Star Wars Funday Football” alt-cast
 Disney+ : Simulcast of main telecast; “Star Wars Funday Football” alt-cast
 Why “Star Wars”? 
 Disney’s content vault is deep, and choosing IP for an event as big as the Super Bowl was a deliberative process. Something animated in the world of “Star Wars” often came up at ESPN and Disney, but with that franchise primarily around live-action content, there needed to be a lot of thought given to how an execution could work.
 “It had to be the right event, and we had to have the assets to really do right by it,” said Michael “ Spike ” Szykowny , ESPN’s VP/edit, animation, graphics innovation and creative production. “When we got to the Super Bowl, the NFL really liked the idea of ‘Star Wars’ and that was something that they would have liked to have seen us do.”
 Once the NFL showed interest, ESPN reached out to its sister divisions Lucasfilm and Industrial Light and Magic, and it just so happened that those folks had some things in the works.
 “Serendipitously, they had characters they were working on. They called them ‘Lils’ and they’re actually animated cartoon character interpretations of the characters from ‘A New Hope,’” noted Szykowny. “So they had been doing that and have these characters that they had started working on, we’re looking at them and go, ‘Wow, this fits perfectly for what we’re thinking about.’”
 “Star Wars Funday Football” also will arrive as Lucasfilm celebrates 50 years of “Star Wars.” Five days after Super Bowl LXI on Feb. 19, a newly restored version of the original 1977 Episode IV (“A New Hope”) will return to theaters. The alt-cast will likely serve as a calling card for Season 2 of “Ahsoka,” which premieres on Disney+ on Jan. 20. Another logical tie-in is the promotion of the first “Star Wars” feature film since 2019: “Starfighter,” which stars Ryan Gosling and is set for release in theaters on May 28.
 “It’s almost hard to believe that you get to do something like this, quite honestly,” Szykowny said. “Everyone that works on this knows how special it is, what a super cool opportunity it is. … We started very small, but nobody knew what these things were when we did our first one. We didn’t even know what it was.
 “We’ve had a bunch of highly successful ones leading up to this with our partners, the NBA, the NHL and NFL. And to me, I think this is a culmination of all that we’ve learned, all that we’ve done in all of these leading up to what is the biggest sporting stage on the planet, arguably, and one of the biggest IPs with a huge fan base that’s out there in the world.”
